Phone / tablet: ◀ ▶ bottom-left to steer (or tilt the phone, in Settings). GAS and BRAKE bottom-right. In the air, hold GAS to drop the nose or BRAKE to lift it. Top-right buttons: respawn, camera, pause.
Time Trial: ride any of the 28 tracks alone. Your best lap is replayed as a blue ghost bike, and the number under TIME TRIAL shows if you are ahead (green) or behind (red) at that point on the lap. The top 10 times on every track go on the Leaderboards.
Helmet cam: press C (or Y) until you are inside the helmet. You see what the rider sees: the visor and chin bar, the screen and the dash with the revs, gear and speed. Your head stays more upright than the bike and looks through the corner, you tuck in behind the bubble on the straights and sit up under braking, and the wind buffets you at speed. Press V to hide the visor frame.
Split times: in a time trial each lap is split into sectors (three on a circuit; on the TT the real timing points at Glen Helen, Ballaugh, Ramsey, the Bungalow and Cronk-ny-Mona). At every split you see your time against the world lap record (or your own best when there's no record or you're offline): purple is faster than the record, green your best yet, amber slower. The results show your best lap sector by sector, and where the most time is.
Telemetry and brake boards: after a time trial on a circuit, the results show your best lap's speed trace over the world record's, with the time gap underneath and the corners where you lost the most. Out on track, the 300, 200 and 100 boards count down to every big braking zone.
Sidecars: pick the Sidecar F2 600 in the Garage (Road tab) and the whole field races outfits, TT-style. A sidecar doesn't lean: your passenger throws his weight out over the chair wheel in left-handers and over the back in right-handers. It sticks like glue in the corners but tops out at about 152 mph, and it won't wheelie.
Rider & Helmet: on the main menu, pick your race number, your bike's colours, your leathers and your helmet colours and design. A turning preview shows the result, and your look goes on your bike in every mode.
Photo mode: in any replay, press 📷 Photo. The replay pauses and you can drag to move the camera around the bike, scroll or pinch to zoom, set the lens and tilt, pick a look (Vivid, B&W, Vintage, Cool) and add focus blur, then save the picture.
Daily challenge: every day there is one new challenge for everyone: a track, a stock bike (no garage upgrades, so it is fair) and the weather. Ride it as often as you like; your best time of the day goes on that day's world board. A new one starts at midnight UTC.
Championship: a ten-round British season, from Oulton Park to the Brands Hatch GP finale. Each weekend starts with qualifying: set your fastest valid lap and that decides your grid slot against the other riders' times (skip it and you start from the back). Points go 25-20-16-13-11-10-9-8, the weather is forecast per round, and your rival is the rider just ahead of you in the table. He raises his game against you. Win the title for a big credits bonus.
Flags and track limits: when a rider goes down, the marshals wave yellow (double waved at the post nearest the crash) and show green once you're past. Overtaking a rider under yellow flags costs a 2-second penalty. On circuits, both tyres past the kerb is a track-limits offence: in a time trial the lap is invalid and the run isn't counted; in a race you get three warnings, then 2 seconds each time.
Racing line (L): on the circuits the line is the minimum-curvature line: wide on the entry, clip the apex, out to the edge on the exit, using the track out to the kerbs. Green is throttle, yellow is lift, red is brake.
Replays: after a time trial, tap Watch replay to see your best lap of the session; if you set a world lap record you can watch your record lap. On the track screen and the world leaderboards, 🎬 plays back anyone's saved lap. The Director cuts between cameras like a TV broadcast: trackside cameras with long lenses at the corners, drones, a helicopter, tracking shots, the tail, front and tank cams, a fly-by on the straights and your helmet cam, finishing low at the line in slow motion. Or pick one camera yourself. Keys: Space pause · ← → skip 5 s · C / X next or previous camera · 1–5 or R speed · Esc exit. Controller: A pause, B exit, LB/RB camera, d-pad skip, Y speed.
Grip and rider aids: lean hard and open the throttle and the rear will slide; let it slide too far and you lowside, snap the throttle shut while sideways and you highside. You can trail-brake: keep braking as you lean into a corner and the bike holds most of its lean, sharing grip between turning and stopping, so it slows a little less hard than upright. On Low or High aids the ABS stops the front tucking; with aids off, a big handful of brake at full lean tucks the front. In the dry, full throttle in low gears pulls a wheelie (ease off or you loop it); in the wet the rear just spins. Rider aids (Settings) catch most of this: High, Low (default) or Off. The yellow TC light shows when they step in.
Tyres: the two bars by the speedo are your front and rear tyre temperatures. Blue is cold, with less grip, so take the first lap steady while they come in. Green is the working window (about 85–110°C in the dry, lower on wets). Amber and red are overheating: sliding and spinning the rear cooks it, and grip fades. Tyres wear as the race goes on, faster if you slide them. Turn it off in Settings if you prefer.
Weather: pick it on the track screen before a race. Rain and snow mean less grip (brake earlier), fog hides the track ahead, and wind gusts push you sideways, hardest in the air. The computer riders slow down too.
Racing line: switch it on in Settings (or press L). Faint dots show the fastest line: green = full throttle, amber = ease off through the corner, red = brake.
Online Race: one rider taps Create race and shares the 4-letter code; friends tap Join race and type it in. Up to 8 riders, and empty grid spots can be computer riders. Your Time Trial results also go on the world leaderboards, where you can race anyone's ghost. Times are kept separately for the dry, the wet and snow (fog and wind count as dry), so pick the weather on the track screen to see that board. World times belong to your rider name, so they stay put through updates, and if you reinstall or switch phone just use the same name to carry on with them. Knees and elbows touch down at full lean on road bikes.
Garage: pick your bike for each kind of racing: 125, 250, 400, 600 or 1000 on the road, 125, 250F or 450F for motocross, 250, 400 or 900 scramblers. Small bikes are slower on the straights but lighter, so they corner faster, stop shorter and change direction quicker. Spend credits from racing on tyres, exhausts, brakes and engine work; each bike keeps its own upgrades and you can swap back to any level you own. Dirt bikes choose tyres for the ground instead: Hard-pack, Mud (and any dirt in the rain), Sand paddles, or Studded for snow. With Random weather, a forecast screen lets you change tyres just before the start. Road tyres suit the weather: race slicks are the grippiest in the dry, wets give far more grip in the rain, and studded tyres bite into snow; the track screen warns you if your tyres don't suit the weather. The computer riders ride the same class as you, on stock bikes.
Isle of Man TT: the full 37.73-mile Mountain Course in one lap, about 18 to 20 minutes. Like the real TT you start alone, ten seconds apart, and race the clock: your position is on corrected time, so a rider you catch on the road may still be ahead of you. The North West 200 is the full 8.97-mile Triangle, mass start.
Bend warnings: a small arrow at the top of the screen calls the next bend like a rally co-driver: 6 is a fast kink down to 1 (very tight), then hairpin, with the distance to it. Amber and red arrows mean real braking. "› L4" means another bend follows straight after. On Real Circuits it shows the corner's name too. Turn it off in Settings.
Hitting barriers at a steep angle, animals, people or traffic will throw you off. Land jumps with the bike matching the slope. Finish in the top 3 to unlock the next round.
Brands Hatch, Cadwell Park, Donington Park, Silverstone, Oulton Park, Snetterton, Thruxton, Castle Combe and Pembrey are surveyed: layout © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), heights, widths, ground and trees from the Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM (© Environment Agency 2022, Open Government Licence v3.0), prepared by Wreckfest-RealCircuits (MIT). Real-circuit outlines: Silverstone from the TUM racetrack database (OpenStreetMap data, LGPL-3.0); Mugello and Losail from bacinger/f1-circuits (MIT). Isle of Man TT Mountain Course: full 37.73-mile road line from OpenStreetMap relation 188240, © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). The North West 200 is full length, traced from the course map. Other real circuits are traced approximations; the Ulster GP is scaled down.
